question: Which Australian vessel participated in Exercise Malabar, 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**HMAS Stuart**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **HMAS Stuart** is an Anzac-class frigate of the Royal Australian Navy (RAN).
 
• HMAS Stuart was commissioned into the RAN in 2002.
 
• HMAS Stuart has participated in numerous international naval exercises, including Exercise Malabar.
 
• Exercise Malabar is a multilateral naval exercise involving the United States, Japan, India, and Australia.
 
• HMAS Stuart's participation in Exercise Malabar strengthens defense ties and interoperability among the participating navies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exercise Malabar:**

 
 
• Originally a bilateral exercise between the United States and India, it expanded to include Japan in 2015 and Australia in 2020.
 
• Exercise Malabar aims to enhance maritime cooperation and promote stability and security in the Indo-Pacific region.
 
• The exercise includes a variety of activities, such as anti-submarine warfare, air defense, and surface warfare drills.
 
 
 
• **Anzac-class Frigates:**
 
 
• The Anzac-class frigates are a class of eight frigates operated by the Royal Australian Navy and two by the Royal New Zealand Navy.
 
• These frigates are designed for a wide range of missions, including anti-submarine warfare, anti-aircraft warfare, and surface combat.
 
 
 
• **Royal Australian Navy (RAN):**
 
 
• The RAN is the naval branch of the Australian Defense Force.
 
• Founded in 1911, the RAN plays a crucial role in securing Australia's maritime interests.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Pacific Security:**
 
 
• The Indo-Pacific region is of strategic importance due to its economic and geopolitical significance.
 
• Naval exercises like Malabar contribute to the collective security and stability of the region.
